newsitem.title: UKRAINE: No money to resurface second Kiev airport runway.
newsitem.headline: No money to resurface second Kiev airport runway.

text.p: Resurfacing work on the second runway at Kiev's international Boryspil airport has been halted because of a disruption in government financing, a top airport official said on Wednesday.
Boris Shakhsuvarov, the airport's First Deputy Director, said the goverment had allocated 35 million hryvnia ($19.8 million) for the work but less than a third had been disbursed.
"Financing has been stopped. The government has no money and we were forced to stop the work," Shakhsuvarov said by telephone.
"We are not seeking non-government credits. We hope the government will come up with the money to finish the job."

The second runaway, built in the 1970s, was to have been brought back into service by mid-1997. But Shakhsuvarov said this was unlikely to happen before the end of next year. Boryspil's main runway is to be renovated in 1998.
"We have no choice but to complete the renovation," he said. "No international airport can operate with the only one runaway."
About 30 airlines, including most major European carriers, fly regularly into Boryspil, which itself underwent major renovations two years ago.

The runway problem was graphically illustrated last year when Boryspil was shut down for more than two hours to allow a plane carrying Ukraine's Defence Minister to make an emergency landing after it lost a wheel on take-off.

Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace is supplying air traffic control equipment for the second runaway worth 30 million German marks ($20 million) but airport authorities have fallen behind in the payments schedule.
